name: CH32V003 RISC-V Microcontroller
summary: A 48 MHz RISC-V part that costs about ten cents, runs from 2.7 to 5.5 V and needs one capacitor to start. Programmed over a single wire.
notes: PD1 is SWIO, the entire debug and programming interface. One wire, no SWCLK. Reassigning it as a GPIO works and costs you the debugger: recovering needs a WCH-LinkE and its unbrick routine, so leave it alone until the firmware is finished.
PD7 comes up as NRST, not as a GPIO. You can free it in the option bytes, and then you have no reset pin.

Only four pins are 5 V tolerant: PC1, PC2, PC5 and PC6. Everything else wants to stay inside VDD even though the chip itself runs happily at 5 V. PC7 is not tolerant, which surprises people wiring SPI, because MOSI is and MISO is not.
PA1 and PA2 double as OSCI and OSCO for an external 24 MHz crystal. The internal RC oscillator is good enough for almost everything, including USART, so most designs keep both as GPIO.
16 KB of flash and 2 KB of SRAM, with the whole 18-pin I/O set on three partial ports: PA has two pins, PC has eight, PD has eight.
The core is RV32EC: sixteen registers rather than thirty-two, and no hardware multiply or divide on this part. Code built for a full RV32I target will not run.
A0 through A7 are ADC channels, not port numbers, and they do not line up with the port pin numbers. A0 is on PA2 and A1 is on PA1, which reads backwards the first time.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit to run

parts.why: The whole of WCH's reference power supply circuit. One capacitor across VDD and VSS, close to the pins.
On NRST, for noise immunity. The pull-up is internal, so this is the only external part the reset pin ever needs.

circuit.note: There is no crystal here and no reset resistor. The oscillator is internal, the reset pull-up is internal, and programming is one wire to PD1. This is close to the smallest part count any 32-bit MCU asks for.

pins.name: PD5
pins.note: Default USART TX, so this is the pin a serial bootloader or printf lands on.

pins.name: PD7
pins.note: Reset after power-up. Becomes a GPIO only if you change the option bytes, and then nothing resets the chip but power.

pins.name: PA1
pins.note: Crystal input if you fit one. ADC channel 1, not 0.

pins.name: PA2
pins.note: Crystal output if you fit one. ADC channel 0.

pins.name: PC4
pins.note: MCO can output the system clock, which is the easy way to prove the PLL is doing what you think.

pins.name: PC7
pins.note: Not 5 V tolerant, unlike the other three SPI pins.

pins.name: PD1
pins.note: The programming pin. Keep a header on it.
